prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens reloaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired stored token as still valid, the proactive pre-request refresh check is skipped, and the client only discovers the token is dead when the server returns 401 — at which point the existing code falls straight through to full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens reloaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time recomputed, so is_token_valid() treats an already-expired stored token as still valid, the proactive pre-request refresh check is skipped, and the client only discovers the token is dead when the server returns 401 — at which point the existing code falls straight through to full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the root cause directly in _initialize(): recomputes token_expiry_time from the stored token's expires_in as soon as it's loaded, so the existing proactive-refresh check in async_auth_flow works correctly and the 401 never happens in the first place. prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same root cause in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing that previously matched fields as raw substrings/regex, which could false-positive across quoted values or comma-separated auth-params. Both introduce a near-identical tokenizer that splits the header on top-level commas while tracking quote state and backslash escapes (PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` vs PR #3041's `_split_www_authenticate_segments`), replacing the old substring/regex-based field extraction. (2 PRs)

Both introduce a near-identical tokenizer that splits the header on top-level commas while tracking quote state and backslash escapes (PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` vs PR #3041's `_split_www_authenticate_segments`), replacing the old substring/regex-based field extraction. prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041 goes a step further than PR #3012: after splitting the header into comma-delimited segments, it adds `_extract_bearer_auth_params` which explicitly identifies which segment starts a new 'Bearer' challenge by partitioning on the scheme token. prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json`: the original check `field_info.annotation is not str` causes JSON pre-parsing to run for ANY annotation other than exactly `str`, including unions like `str | None`. This corrupts plain string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. numeric-looking or JSON-object-looking strings) when the field actually accepts a string. Both add a helper to decide when pre-parsing should be skipped for union-with-str annotations. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in `pre_parse_json`: the original check `field_info.annotation is not str` causes JSON pre-parsing to run for ANY annotation other than exactly `str`, including unions like `str | None`. This corrupts plain string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. numeric-looking or JSON-object-looking strings) when the field actually accepts a string. Both add a helper to decide when pre-parsing should be skipped for union-with-str annotations. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3056 additionally strips `Annotated[...]` wrappers from each union member via `_unwrap_annotated` before comparing types. This matters because the common MCP tool-definition pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` nests the Annotated wrapper inside the union args (pydantic only strips a top-level Annotated, not per-member). PR #2032's `_SIMPLE_TYPES` membership check compares raw union args directly against `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}`, so an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` arg fails that membership test and is treated as a 'complex' type — meaning the original corruption bug persists for described optional string parameters, a common signature style in this codebase. #3056's narrower but more precise handling closes that gap; #2032's broader primitive-union coverage (e.g. `int | float | bool` combos) is a nice-to-have but doesn't address the Annotated case actually hit in practice.

prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, OAuthContext has a refresh_token loaded from storage but no authorization-server metadata in memory, so refresh_token() has no way to resolve the token endpoint and cold-start token refresh breaks. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a process restart, OAuthContext has a refresh_token loaded from storage but no authorization-server metadata in memory, so refresh_token() has no way to resolve the token endpoint and cold-start token refresh breaks. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Resolves cold-start refresh by re-running the existing AS metadata discovery pipeline on demand before refreshing, adds an issuer-binding check on the (re)discovered metadata to guard against a substituted/rotated authorization server, and tracks eager_discovery_attempted so servers that publish no metadata aren't re-probed on every refresh — all without changing any public interfaces. #2492 instead adds two new methods (get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata) to the public TokenStorage protocol, meaning every existing TokenStorage implementation has to be updated to actually benefit, and it caches metadata indefinitely with no check that the persisted metadata still matches the issuer if the AS configuration changes later.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 goes a step further than PR #3012: after splitting the header into comma-delimited segments, it adds `_extract_bearer_auth_params` which explicitly identifies which segment starts a new 'Bearer' challenge by partitioning on the scheme token. PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of params, so it does not correctly isolate a Bearer challenge from other schemes/challenges that may appear later in the same header (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...'). #3041's scheme-aware segmentation handles that multi-challenge case that #3012's simpler split does not.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3056 additionally strips `Annotated[...]` wrappers from each union member via `_unwrap_annotated` before comparing types. This matters because the common MCP tool-definition pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` nests the Annotated wrapper inside the union args (pydantic only strips a top-level Annotated, not per-member). PR #2032's `_SIMPLE_TYPES` membership check compares raw union args directly against `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}`, so an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` arg fails that membership test and is treated as a 'complex' type — meaning the original corruption bug persists for described optional string parameters, a common signature style in this codebase. #3056's narrower but more precise handling closes that gap; #2032's broader primitive-union coverage (e.g. `int | float | bool` combos) is a nice-to-have but doesn't address the Annotated case actually hit in practice.

This corrupts plain string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. numeric-looking or JSON-object-looking strings) when the field actually accepts a string. clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 goes a step further than PR #3012: after splitting the header into comma-delimited segments, it adds `_extract_bearer_auth_params` which explicitly identifies which segment starts a new 'Bearer' challenge by partitioning on the scheme token. PR #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` only finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of params, so it does not correctly isolate a Bearer challenge from other schemes/challenges that may appear later in the same header (e.g. 'Bearer ..., DPoP ...'). #3041's scheme-aware segmentation handles that multi-challenge case that #3012's simpler split does not.
